structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E061. The tip is E061: 5.024 s / 0.7534, with 225 steps and seeds 0-2 sitting on the bar.
1. Accuracy noise: per-seed SD is about 0.25 pp and the 3-seed SD about 0.15 pp. The build component is about 0 (E057/E059). A recipe whose population mean is about 0.7535 passes the 0.753 gate about half the time, so any lever that costs more than about 0.1 pp usually fails seeds 0-2.
2. A new mechanism explains my time misses (E056, E059, E061). Low-resolution steps are bound by host overhead and fixed per-step work, not by pixels. Removing 12 steps at 20 px saved about 0.15 s, about 12 ms per step, which is roughly twice their conv compute. Each step pays for Python LR-setting loops over about 9 param groups, 3 compiled Muon calls (each a cudagraph replay plus an lr_t fill), fused SGD, a Lookahead every 5 steps, and slicing and indexing. All of this runs on 4 pinned CPU cores. The GPU catches up at 28/32 px but idles at 20/24 px. Session-level drift in this host overhead also explains why identical code reads 5.08 to 5.22. Consequences: (a) levers that remove steps or optimizer calls save more than FLOP accounting predicts, especially early; (b) levers that only change per-pixel arithmetic, such as activations, save less than predicted unless they change the compiled step's memory traffic, as ReLU's bool mask did in E056.
3. Accuracy is carried by optimizer steps on layers that are still learning. Lowering early pixels at a fixed step count is free (E026, E033). Removing steps costs about the dial's rate (E031, E041, E045). E061's re-test passed only because the dial's price fell. Freezes are free only once a layer's learning has finished: the whitening bias by about 6% (E060), the stem at 75%, group 2 at about 90%. Earlier freezes cost accuracy (E037, E054, E055).
4. Freezes beat their FLOP share by skipping BN/GELU backward and the Muon calls. Under item 2 this is partly saved host and launch work, not just bytes.
5. The end-game is at a local optimum: averaging, LS and LR-floor tweaks all hurt or were null.
6. Settled by reading the code: the BN scale is frozen, filter wd is inert because Muon renormalizes, and only fine labels are supplied.
7. Muon vs SGD: E006 is confounded, and PR #3 favours SGD. But this recipe's freeze anneals, wd ×0.5 and lr were all tuned under renormalized Muon filters, so dropping SGD in untuned should lose 0.3-0.6 pp. It saves 3 Muon calls per step, which is worth more than the NS FLOPs (about 0.15-0.25 s).
8. The PCIe judge's times will be 5-10% higher, and more so if the judge's host is slower.
Unsure about: how large host-bound per-step overhead really is (one CUDA-event versus wall-time trace at 20 px would settle it); whether the batch can grow early without losing steps' worth of accuracy; whether Muon's advantage is real.

forecasts.reason: Removing the 3 Muon calls per step saves both host and NS time (about 0.17 s). But the freeze anneals and wd were tuned under renormalized Muon filters, so untuned SGD loses about 0.4 pp.

ReLU's saving came from its bool-mask backward. tanh-GELU and SiLU still save fp16 inputs, and the steps are partly host-bound, so the projected saving is under 1.5%. Most likely closed with no run, or a run within noise.
Early steps are overhead-bound, so cutting about 28 low-res steps saves more than their pixel share (about 0.13 s). But steps carry accuracy (H5.2), so it loses about 0.2 pp.

cruxes: Is the 20/24 px step bound by host overhead? Compare per-step CUDA-event GPU busy time with wall time at 20 px. If GPU busy is under 60%, consolidating the 4 optimizer calls into one graph and cutting the per-step Python LR loops is the cheapest identical-math lever left.
Does Muon carry real accuracy at batch 2000 on this freeze-tuned recipe, or was E006's gain from batch size and an RNG re-draw?
Is session-level time drift (±2%) larger than the effects now being chased? Without repeated sessions, sub-2% time keeps are draws.
